src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2024_us_cd119_500k
cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 119th Congress's districts (its file says session 119).
rec: 2022 congressional plan adopted by the Wisconsin Supreme Court: the Governor's plan (Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, 2022 WI 14, 'Johnson II')

Wisconsin Statutes ch. 3 (2021-22), note: the Act 44 plan is superseded by Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, 2022 WI 14, and the court-approved plan first applies to the 2022 general election

The Johnson II congressional plan was used again; the 2023 Clarke decision and Act 94 concerned legislative districts only, and the Wisconsin Supreme Court declined to reopen the congressional plan. Census check: cb_2024_us_cd119 (CDSESSN 119; lines supplied by the states by May 31, 2024); 0 of 8 districts differ in shape from the 2022 file.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2024_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2024 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2024 legislative session year.
rec: 2023 Wisconsin Act 94 legislative plan (the Governor's remedial maps, enacted after Clarke v. WEC, 2023 WI 79)
Wisconsin Statutes ch. 4 (2023-24): the Senate and Assembly districts are those of 2023 Wisconsin Act 94

The Wisconsin Supreme Court held on Dec. 22, 2023 that the Johnson III districts violated the contiguity requirement and ordered new maps before 2024; the Legislature passed 2023 Senate Bill 488 on Feb. 13, 2024 (identical to the Governor's remedial maps) and the Governor signed it Feb. 19, 2024 as 2023 Wisconsin Act 94. Half the Senate (odd-numbered districts) was elected in 2024. The Census file carries a 'ZZZ' record for area the state assigned to no district. Census check: cb_2024_55_sldu (LSY 2024, 34 districts; boundaries collected for the 2024 election year); 31 of 34 districts differ in shape from the 2022 file.

New Assembly districts for 2024 (Act 94, signed Feb. 19, 2024); the Johnson III districts were enjoined by Clarke v. WEC. The Census file carries a 'ZZZ' record for area the state assigned to no district. Census check: cb_2024_55_sldl (LSY 2024, 100 districts; boundaries collected for the 2024 election year); 89 of 100 districts differ in shape from the 2022 file.
